findings.claim: --output-groups now defaults to the --build-jobs value, or to the -j value if --build-jobs is not given. svsim's '--build-jobs 0' resolves to std::thread::hardware_concurrency(), so on the 4-CPU box output grouping is turned on with 4 groups. svsim's default '-j 0' behaves the same way. In 5.034 the default was 0, meaning grouping was off. All svsim jobs flags remain valid and nothing else about -j, --build-jobs or --verilate-jobs changed.
findings.evidence: Changes 5.036 **Important**: "Change `--output-groups` to default to value of `--build-jobs` (#5751). Those using build farms may need to now use `--output-groups 0` or otherwise." Commits d2329230 and 2455d152. v5.036:src/V3Options.h:327 `int m_outputGroups = -1;` (was 0). v5.036:src/V3Options.cpp:963 `if (m_outputGroups == -1) m_outputGroups = (m_buildJobs != -1) ? m_buildJobs : 0;` and :1853 (-j path) `if (m_outputGroups == -1) m_outputGroups = val;`. :1202-1203 --build-jobs 0 gives `val = std::thread::hardware_concurrency();`. Grouping only applies above thresholds: v5.036:src/V3EmitMk.cpp:62 `MIN_FILES_COUNT = 16`, :66 `MIN_FILES_PER_BUCKET = 4`, :185-191 fallbackNoGrouping. Docs: "Negative one, the default, sets the groups to the value from --build-jobs, or from -j, or zero in that priority."
findings.impact: Moderate for build time, none for simulation results. The generated .cpp files of the model (VM_CLASSES fast and slow) are combined into about N=hardware_concurrency 'vm_classes_*.cpp' / 'vm_classes_Slow_*.cpp' units. This only happens when a set has at least 16 files and at least 4*N files, so small ChiselSim designs are unaffected. The generated file list now depends on the CPU count of the build machine, which affects reproducibility and ccache hits. '--output-groups 0' restores the 5.034 behavior.
findings.expected_measurement: For tests whose verilated-sources hold 16 or more model .cpp files, look for new vm_classes_*.cpp concatenation files and a changed C++ build time compared with 5.034. Otherwise expect the same file list. Exit codes and simulation outputs should not change.

findings.claim: Nothing in the verilator_bin thread pool, the mutexes or the exit path changed between v5.034 and v5.036. The exit-race behavior (upstream issue 4931) of 5.036 should therefore match 5.034's, both with '-j 0' and with '--build-jobs 0 --verilate-jobs 1'.
findings.evidence: `git diff v5.034 v5.036 -- src/V3ThreadPool.cpp src/V3ThreadPool.h src/V3Mutex.h` is empty (0 lines). The v5.034..v5.036 src/Verilator.cpp diff only adds `#include "V3EmitMkJson.h"` and `"V3Udp.h"`, `if (v3Global.hasTable()) V3Udp::udpResolve(...)` and `if (v3Global.opt.makeJson()) V3EmitMkJson::emit();`. No src/ diff line mentions ThreadPool, std::thread, V3Mutex or exit(.
findings.impact: 5.036 has whatever abort rate 5.034 has. The '--verilate-jobs 1' workaround stays equally valid.
findings.expected_measurement: Abort count ('attempted to destroy locked Thread Pool', exit 255) per 3000 verilations should be statistically the same as the 5.034 measurement for both flag sets.

findings.claim: The $urandom/$random runtime, +verilator+seed+ parsing, randReset and the default-seed path are unchanged in this range, and also unchanged since v5.020. Without a seed, runs should stay identical: randSeed()==0 uses unseeded lrand48 through vl_sys_rand32. Seed 1 should give the same values as 5.020, as long as the design makes the same RNG calls. The new resetting of automatic function locals uses zero-init, not VL_RAND_RESET, so it does not consume RNG values.
findings.evidence: `git diff v5.034 v5.036 -- include/ src/ | grep '^[-+].*(randSeed|vl_rand64|VL_RANDOM|randReset|seed|urandom|VL_RAND_RESET)'` returns nothing. `git diff v5.020 v5.036 -- include/verilated.cpp | grep '^[-+].*(rand|seed|Seed)'` also returns nothing; in verilated.h only declarations were reordered. v5.036:include/verilated.cpp:2877 `commandArgVlUint64(arg, "+verilator+seed+", u64, 1, std::numeric_limits<int>::max())` (seed 0 is still rejected). :2943-2949 randSeedDefault64 uses `(seed<<32)^seed`, otherwise vl_sys_rand32(). VlRNG::vl_thread_rng inverts states with fewer than 10 one bits, which explains the many 1 bits seen with seed 1. v5.036:src/V3EmitCFunc.cpp zeroit includes `|| varp->isFuncLocal()  // Randomization too slow`.
findings.expected_measurement: No seed: 48c2e0e4 9efdd502 0b1e5d9c 797673c4 in every run. +verilator+seed+1: 8084023f f77f7fff ff7fffff fffffffc. +verilator+seed+2: f1080460 eeff3fff feffffff fffffffa. +verilator+seed+0 still rejected.

findings.claim: New warning DEFOVERRIDE, on by default. It fires whenever source code `defines a macro that was already defined on the command line, even with the same value. The source definition is then ignored and the command-line value wins. In 5.034 the later source `define replaced the command-line value, and only a different value raised REDEFMACRO. Without -Wno-fatal, which svsim does not pass, any DEFOVERRIDE makes verilation fail.
findings.evidence: Changes 5.036: "Support command-line overriding `define (#5900) (#5908). [Brian Li]", commit 559d990e. v5.036:src/V3Error.h:93 `DEFOVERRIDE,    // Overriding existing define macro through command line`. It is not in defaultsOff(), lintError() or styleError(). v5.036:src/V3PreProc.cpp:354 `if (defCmdline(name) && !cmdline) { fl->v3warn(DEFOVERRIDE, "Overriding define: '" ...); return; }`, which keeps the command-line definition with no value comparison.
findings.impact: Low. svsim passes +define+ for ASSERT_VERBOSE_COND, PRINTF_COND, STOP_COND, the layer$... macros, RANDOMIZE_REG_INIT/MEM_INIT, RANDOMIZE_DELAY and RANDOM. 5.020 produced no REDEFMACRO, so the firtool output never redefines these with a different value, and firtool's standard headers guard them with `ifndef. Only an unguarded same-value `define of one of these macros would newly break the build. Command-line priority cannot change RANDOM=$urandom unless the source redefines it unguarded.
findings.expected_measurement: No %Warning-DEFOVERRIDE (and no %Warning at all) in the 53 ChiselSim builds of sbt test.

findings.claim: The 'previous value' variables used for edge and change detection are now initialized in _eval_static, before initial blocks run. Before, they were set at the end of _eval_initial. As a result, a posedge or negedge caused by an initial block at time 0 now triggers logic. Changed/hybrid sensitivities such as svsim's `always @(simulationState)` already fire on the first evaluation through the DidInit trigger, so the harness start-up is unaffected.
findings.evidence: Changes 5.036: "Fix change detection at time 0 (#5499) (#5864). [Geza Lore]", commit 4a221294 ("Initialize 'previous value' variables in the static initializer function, instead of the 'initial' blocks function"). v5.036:src/V3Sched.cpp:459 `AstCFunc* createStatic(...)` now returns the function used as initFuncp. :1239 `createSettle(netlistp, staticp, ...)`, and the act/ico triggers likewise use staticp. :717 `if (pair.second || v3Global.opt.xInitialEdge())` marks the initial firing only for changed/hybrid terms. svsim's Workspace template has `initial simulationState = RUN; always @(simulationState) ... simulation_body();`.
findings.impact: Probably none for this project. clock and reset are driven only through svsim DPI calls after time 0. firtool's RANDOMIZE_REG_INIT initial blocks write data registers, not clocks or async resets. A design that derives a clock or async reset from a register randomized in an initial block could see an extra edge at time 0.
findings.expected_measurement: Same pass/fail results, cycle counts and printed output as 5.034/5.020 for the same seed.

findings.claim: Fixes a miscompile, present in 5.030 to 5.034, in the 'FlagShared' NBA scheme used for unpacked arrays of packed elements, such as firtool memories `reg [w:0] Memory[0:d]`. When consecutive NBAs to different array variables in the same always block shared a __VdlySet flag, the second variable reused the first variable's commit `if` block, so commits could be lost or misplaced. 5.020 predates this scheme.
findings.evidence: Changes 5.036: "Fix NBA shared flag reuse (#5848). [Geza Lore]", commit 6ecdd14f (fixes #5847). The bug was introduced by 5acced1e3 "Refactor V3Delay for extensibility (#5516)", first released in v5.030 (`git describe --contains` gives v5.030~39). v5.036:src/V3Delayed.cpp:479 `// Different variable, ensure the commit block exists for this variable,` adds a new commitFlagp per variable. :273 `if (basicp) return Scheme::FlagShared;` applies to arrays of packed/basic elements. Test t_nba_shared_flag_reuse.v has `addr[0] <= ...; len[0] <= ...;` in one always block.
findings.impact: Low. firtool usually emits one memory per module, so consecutive NBAs in one always block hit the same array; the same-variable case is unchanged. This matters only if two memory arrays are written in the same always block. It removes a correctness risk relative to 5.030-5.034.
findings.expected_measurement: Same results as 5.020. Any test that differed on 5.030-5.034 because of memory-write corruption should match 5.020 again.

findings.claim: Automatic function and task local variables without an initializer are now reset to their default at every call. Before, they could keep stale values from the previous call. Function locals are zero-initialized, not randomized.
findings.evidence: Changes 5.036: "Fix reset of automatic function variables (#5747). [Augustin Fabre]", commit 3b98db17. src/V3Task.cpp: `if (portp->needsCReset() && portp->lifetime().isAutomatic() && !portp->valuep()) { ... portp->replaceWith(new AstCReset{portp->fileline(), vrefp, false}); }`. src/V3EmitCFunc.cpp zeroit includes `varp->isFuncLocal()`.
findings.impact: Negligible. firtool output for synchronous RTL has no SV functions with read-before-write locals. The change does not consume RNG values.
findings.expected_measurement: n/a. No change in results expected.

findings.claim: New default-on optimization -fvar-split. It automatically splits packed variables that are only accessed through constant, non-overlapping bit or range selects, which can remove UNOPTFLAT cases and change the generated code. '-fno-var-split' or -O0 turns it off.
findings.evidence: Changes 5.036: "Optimize automatic splitting of some packed variables (#5843). [Geza Lore]", commit d9701e64 ("attempts to split up packed variables that are only referenced via constant index, non-overlapping bit/range selects. This can eliminate some UNOPTFLAT cases."). v5.036:src/V3Options.cpp:1357 `DECL_OPTION("-fvar-split", FOnOff, &m_fVarSplit);`, :2182 `m_fVarSplit = flag;` (optimize(1) is the default). v5.036:src/V3SplitVar.cpp:1321 `if (v3Global.opt.fVarSplit()) { ... findCandidates(...) }`.
findings.impact: Low to moderate. firtool output often uses constant part-selects of wide _GEN wires and registers, so both verilation time and simulation runtime may shift slightly. Results should be unchanged.
findings.expected_measurement: Small changes, in either direction, in verilation and simulation wall time compared with 5.034. Same results, and no new warnings.

findings.claim: No new toolchain requirement for building from source on Ubuntu 24.04: configure.ac only adds an optional clang flag and changes how tcmalloc is linked. With the default --enable-partial-static, a static libtcmalloc_minimal.a is now linked with --whole-archive, so tcmalloc really replaces malloc in verilator_bin. Before, with mold and -gc-sections, it could be silently dropped. Ubuntu 24.04 gcc and clang are CI build/test targets; Ubuntu 20.04 CI was turned off.
findings.evidence: Changes 5.036: "Fix tcmalloc static link and non-22.04 builds (#5817) (#5818). [Geza Lore]", commit 99064d3e "Make mold static link tcmalloc". v5.034..v5.036 configure.ac diff: `-  LTCMALLOC=-l:libtcmalloc_minimal.a` / `+  LTCMALLOC="-Wl,--whole-archive -l:libtcmalloc_minimal.a -Wl,--no-whole-archive"`, plus `_MY_CXX_CHECK_OPT(CFG_CXXFLAGS_SRC,-Xclang -fno-pch-timestamp)` (applied only if the compiler accepts it). v5.036:.github/workflows/build.yml:36 `{os: ubuntu-24.04, cc: gcc}`. Commit d31bce91 "Actions: Turn off Ubuntu 20.04".
findings.impact: Building from source on Ubuntu 24.04 with g++ 13 works as before. If libgoogle-perftools-dev (and mold) are installed, verilator_bin now actually uses tcmalloc, which can speed up verilation compared with a 5.034 source build. The Debian 5.020 package baseline is not affected.
findings.expected_measurement: configure/make succeeds on Ubuntu 24.04 with the same packages as 5.034. With libgoogle-perftools-dev, `nm`/`ldd` on verilator_bin should show tcmalloc symbols and verilation may be somewhat faster.

findings.claim: Every option and the C++ runtime API that svsim uses still work. '--trace' is now documented as deprecated in favor of '--trace-vcd', but it is still parsed silently and means VCD; svsim's TraceKind.Vcd passes '--trace'. The runtime headers add only a type trait, and the generated model API (eval, eval_step, final, eventsPending, nextTimeSlot, VerilatedContext::*) only changed message text. -std=c++17 remains sufficient.
findings.evidence: Changes 5.036: "Change `--trace` to `--trace-vcd`.", commit 0984fd04. v5.036:src/V3Options.cpp:1643 `DECL_OPTION("-trace", OnOff, &m_trace);` emits no DEPRECATED warning, unlike --xml-only. Docs: ".. option:: --trace / Deprecated; use --trace-fst, --trace-saif or --trace-vcd instead." The v5.034..v5.036 V3Options.cpp diff removes no option used by svsim (--cc --exe --build -o --top-module --Mdir --assert --timescale -CFLAGS +define -F --build-jobs --verilate-jobs). include/verilated.h diff only adds `struct VlContainsCustomStruct`. src/V3EmitCModel.cpp diff changes only the text "--trace" to "--trace-vcd". svsim/verilator/Backend$CompilationSettings$TraceKind$Vcd$.class contains the string "--trace".
findings.impact: None. svsim and simulation-driver.cpp should build unchanged, including VCD tracing.
findings.expected_measurement: All 53 ChiselSim builds succeed with unchanged flags. A traced run still produces a .vcd file.

findings.claim: The VCD writer (and FST likewise) now drops a timestamp line when no value changes follow it, overwriting the duplicate '#<time>'. VCD files from tracing are therefore not byte-identical to 5.034/5.020 output, even though the waveform content is the same. This change is not listed in Changes.
findings.evidence: Commit 34a760b7 "Optimize duplicate timestamps out of traces (#4686)" (touches include/verilated_vcd_c.cpp, include/verilated_fst_c.cpp and many .vcd/.fst golden files). v5.036:include/verilated_vcd_c.cpp:196 `if (m_wrTimeEndp == m_writep) m_writep = m_wrTimeBeginp;` in emitTimeChange.
findings.impact: Only matters if the project diffs trace files across Verilator versions or checks traces byte-for-byte for determinism. Run-to-run determinism within 5.036 is unaffected.
findings.expected_measurement: With tracing on, 5.036 VCDs have fewer '#<time>' lines than 5.034/5.020 VCDs. Repeated 5.036 runs with the same seed give identical VCDs.

research.notes:
There are no intermediate releases: the Changes file goes straight from 5.034 (2025-02-24) to 5.036 (2025-04-27), with 183 commits in v5.034..v5.036. Changes I checked and left out as irrelevant to this project:
- "Add numactl-like automatic assignment of processor affinity (#5911)" is in include/verilated_threads.cpp VlThreadPool::numaAssign. It only acts with 2 or more model worker threads (line 139 `if (num_threads < 2) return "too few threads"`), and svsim does not pass --threads.
- "Optimize trigger vector in whole words (#5857)" speeds up C++ compile only for designs with many (64 or more) triggers, so it is negligible for single-clock ChiselSim designs.
- "Fix invalid code motion over branches (#5811)" only affects disable/return/break code, which firtool does not emit.
- "Fix packed selection using over 32-bit index (#5957)" needs indices wider than 32 bits.
- UDP support, --make json, --trace-saif, multi-thread hierarchical simulation and the expression-coverage COVERIGN all need features svsim does not use.
- V3Error message rewording, v3fatal changed to v3error for bad option values, and the UNOPTFLAT hint text are cosmetic.
- V3Assert/V3AssertPre changed only in code style, with no functional change.
- Besides DEFOVERRIDE, the only new warning is DEPRECATED for --xml-only/--xml-output, which svsim does not use.

Side effect to report: some git commands on the blobless scratch clone (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-deterministic-vliw-chisel/72342c7d-9f6b-5534-9c62-327a6a17dee8/scratchpad/vsrc) set off git's background 'Auto packing' (gc). Later commands used `-c gc.auto=0`, but that one background gc may briefly have used CPU on the measurement box. I did not touch /home/user/deterministic-vliw-chisel, and did not build or run anything.

verdicts.evidence: Verified in the git objects. Changes 5.036 'Important' lists '--output-groups to default to value of --build-jobs (#5751)'. The commits d23292305 and 2455d1527 are in v5.036 and not in v5.034. v5.034 V3Options.h:325 has `m_outputGroups = 0`. v5.036 V3Options.h:327 has `-1`. V3Options.cpp:963 has `if (m_outputGroups == -1) m_outputGroups = (m_buildJobs != -1) ? m_buildJobs : 0;`. The -j path at :1853 sets `m_outputGroups = val`. :1196-1205 resolves `--build-jobs 0` to std::thread::hardware_concurrency(). The docs say 'Negative one, the default, sets the groups to the value from --build-jobs, or from -j, or zero'. The grouping thresholds are real (V3EmitMk.cpp:62 MIN_FILES_COUNT=16, :66 MIN_FILES_PER_BUCKET=4, fallbackNoGrouping at :181-195). Precisely, grouping is skipped if (count<16 && count<=N) or count<4N. For N=4 that means grouping needs 16 or more concatenable files. The fast and slow sets are evaluated separately, and the count is re-checked after excluding oversized and single-file work lists. Group files are named `<prefix>_vm_classes_<n>.cpp` and `<prefix>_vm_classes_Slow_<n>.cpp` (V3EmitMk.cpp:327, :524-526). Nothing else about -j, --build-jobs or --verilate-jobs changed. Docs and error handling only: a negative --build-jobs value is now v3error instead of v3fatal, and the docs drop the misleading '[<value>]'. No option was removed.

`git diff --numstat v5.034 v5.036` for src/V3ThreadPool.cpp, src/V3ThreadPool.h and src/V3Mutex.h prints nothing, so they are byte-identical. A grep of the src+include diff for ThreadPool, std::thread, V3Mutex, exit( and atexit finds only runtime-side VlThreadPool numa code (include/verilated_threads.*, a different library) and whitespace re-indents of exit(255) in include/gtkwave/fstapi.c. The src/Verilator.cpp diff is as described: it adds V3EmitMkJson and V3Udp includes, `if (v3Global.hasTable()) V3Udp::udpResolve(...)`, and the `--make json` emit calls. V3Error.cpp changes only the rename EC_FATALEXIT to EC_FATALMANY plus message text; the exit logic is unchanged. This supports 'same code, so presumably same abort rate'. It is an inference from code identity, not a measurement.

The core is right and stronger than stated. The RNG functions (VlRNG::VlRNG, rand64, vl_thread_rng_rand64, srandom, vl_sys_rand32, vl_thread_rng) hash identically between v5.020 and v5.036 (identical md5 of the extracted functions). v5.036 verilated.cpp:354-363 is vl_sys_rand32 with unseeded lrand48. :367-381 is vl_thread_rng, which inverts states with fewer than 10 one bits. :2943-2949 is randSeedDefault64, which uses (seed<<32)^seed when the seed is nonzero and vl_sys_rand32 otherwise. :2877 parses +verilator+seed+ with minimum 1. No srand call exists anywhere in include/. A case-insensitive grep of the v5.034..v5.036 src+include diff for randSeed, VL_RANDOM, VL_RAND_RESET, seed, urandom, lrand48 and srand returns nothing. No AstRand or x-initial code changed in the range either. The automatic-function reset is zeroed: V3EmitCFunc.cpp:752 `varp->isFuncLocal() // Randomization too slow` is pre-existing and not added by 3b98db17. FLAW in the evidence: the claim 'unchanged since v5.020' rests on a case-sensitive grep that misses uppercase RAND. The 5.020 to 5.036 diff of verilated.cpp does contain additions: VL_RAND_RESET_ASSIGN_I/Q/W (absent in v5.026, present in v5.028; assign-time reset used for unique x-assign) and a changed x/z path in the scanf code (`VL_RAND_RESET_I(m_hex ? 4 : 1)`). Neither touches $urandom, $random, seeding or VL_RAND_RESET_I at init, so the prediction stands.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The $urandom/$random runtime (VlRNG, vl_sys_rand32, vl_thread_rng, randSeedDefault64, VL_RANDOM_*), +verilator+seed+ parsing and the VL_RAND_RESET_I/Q/W init-time path are unchanged between v5.020 and v5.036, and everything in the range v5.034..v5.036 is unchanged. Not true as written: the runtime did gain VL_RAND_RESET_ASSIGN_I/Q/W in 5.028 and a changed x/z path in the scanf code, which the researcher's case-sensitive grep missed. Neither affects the predicted values: without a seed, identical runs; with +verilator+seed+1, the same values as 5.020 provided the design makes the same RNG calls.

verdicts.evidence: v5.036 V3Error.h:93 adds DEFOVERRIDE, and it is added to the names table. It is absent from defaultsOff(), lintError() and styleError(), so it is on by default. The only other warning-code change in V3Error.h is the EC_FATALEXIT rename. A scan of added v3warn call sites in the src diff finds only DEFOVERRIDE, REDEFMACRO (re-wording) and DEPRECATED (xml-only/xml-output). v5.036 V3PreProc.cpp:354 is `if (defCmdline(name) && !cmdline) { v3warn(DEFOVERRIDE, ...); return; }` with no value comparison, so the warning also fires for identical values. v5.034 V3PreProc.cpp:347-363 had only the REDEFMACRO check for differing values, followed by undef and re-add, so the source value won. Commit 559d990e8 (2025-04-01) is in range. The docs entry exists. The impact reasoning (firtool headers guard with `ifndef) cannot be checked from these objects. Also note that 'no REDEFMACRO on 5.020' says nothing about same-value redefinitions, which were silent on 5.020. The risk is therefore an unguarded same-value `define of an svsim +define+ macro, which is rare.

Commit 4a2212949 (2025-03-18) is in range. Its diff to V3Sched.cpp makes createStatic return the _eval_static function, and createInitial no longer returns one. createSettle, createInputCombLoop and createTriggers now take staticp instead of initp. The prev-value init statements therefore move from the end of _eval_initial to _eval_static. The model's first eval runs _eval_static, then _eval_initial, then _eval_settle (V3EmitCModel.cpp:427-432, unchanged). New test t_scheduling_initial_event expects pEdgeCnt==2 with times 0 and 20, so a time-0 initial-block edge now fires. The initial-trigger bit is set only for changed/hybrid terms (V3Sched.cpp:717). svsim's Workspace.class does contain the template `enum {INIT, RUN, DONE} simulationState = INIT; ... simulationState = RUN; always @(simulationState) begin if (simulationState == RUN) ...`. Tracing that case: in both versions the always block fires once at the first eval (as hybrid DidInit in 5.034; as a real INIT to RUN change plus DidInit in 5.036, which is the same trigger bit). The next iteration sees the DONE change and does nothing, so start-up is unaffected. The residual risk (a clock or async reset derived from a register that an initial block randomizes) is correctly flagged as hypothetical.

Commit 6ecdd14fd (2025-03-11) is in range. The FlagShared scheme does not exist in v5.020, v5.026 or v5.028 (0 matches in V3Delayed.cpp) and has 18 matches in v5.030 and v5.034. The refactor 5acced1e3 first appears in v5.030 (git tag --contains lists v5.030 as the earliest tag). The pre-fix code made the second variable take `m_vscpInfo(m_prevVscp).flagSharedKit().commitIfp` unconditionally. The fix adds a per-variable commitFlagp and creates a new commit `if` in that variable's own post block when the variable differs and the flag differs (V3Delayed.cpp:472-495). chooseScheme returns FlagShared for unpacked arrays of basic/packed elements (V3Delayed.cpp:273). The regression test t_nba_shared_flag_reuse has two arrays (addr[], len[]) written non-consecutively in one always block and checks addr[0]. The trigger pattern is therefore multiple array variables with interleaved NBAs in one always block. The impact assessment (firtool memories usually hit the same-variable path) is plausible but not verified.

Commit 3b98db17c (2025-02-25) is in range. src/V3Task.cpp now replaces the localized port/var with `AstCReset{..., false}` when `portp->needsCReset() && portp->lifetime().isAutomatic() && !portp->valuep()`. This emits a per-call reset (non-constructing clear). Previously the CReset ran only at construction. The zeroing is as claimed: V3EmitCFunc.cpp:752 `zeroit` includes `varp->isFuncLocal()`, and that line predates this commit, so no RNG values are consumed. The commit also adds V3Life CRESET elimination, so there is no new UNOPTFLAT or perf cost.

Commit d9701e640 (2025-03-09) is in range. It adds `DECL_OPTION("-fvar-split", FOnOff, &m_fVarSplit)` (V3Options.cpp:1357) and `m_fVarSplit = flag` inside optimize() (:2182). The constructor calls optimize(1) (:2104), so the default is on, and -O0 or -fno-var-split turns it off. V3SplitVar.cpp:1321 gates `findCandidates` on `fVarSplit()`. The commit message says 'attempts to split up packed variables that are only referenced via constant index, non-overlapping bit/range selects. This can eliminate some UNOPTFLAT cases.' The docs (extensions.rst) add 'Packed variables that are only referenced locally (without hierarchical references) via non-overlapping, constant-indexed bit or part select expressions are split automatically'. New stats lines 'SplitVar, packed variables split automatically' exist, and several existing tests had to opt out with -fno-var-split. Results should not change. The size of the performance effect on firtool output is a prediction, not verified.

The v5.034..v5.036 configure.ac diff matches the claim: the version bump, a new `_MY_CXX_CHECK_OPT(CFG_CXXFLAGS_SRC,-Xclang -fno-pch-timestamp)` (an optional flag, only used if the compiler accepts it, so g++ ignores it), and `LTCMALLOC="-Wl,--whole-archive -l:libtcmalloc_minimal.a -Wl,--no-whole-archive"`. The C++ standard selection is unchanged (c++17 newest, c++14 oldest, configure.ac:404-413). The verilog.y diff has no %require or %define lines, so there is no new bison feature. The install.rst changes are reordering only. The new objects V3EmitMkJson.o and V3Udp.o are plain additions to Makefile_obj.in. The CI matrix has ubuntu-24.04 gcc and clang (.github/workflows/build.yml:36), and d31bce915 turns off 20.04. The rationale 'tcmalloc could be silently dropped with mold and -gc-sections' is an inference. The commit message says only 'Make mold static link tcmalloc'.
verdicts.corrected_claim: No new toolchain requirement on Ubuntu 24.04 (g++ 13, python3, flex and bison unchanged, C++14 minimum and C++17 preferred unchanged). The only build change is that the static tcmalloc archive is linked with --whole-archive. The reason (tcmalloc being dropped under mold/-gc-sections) is the researcher's inference, not documented in the commit. Upstream CI installs libgoogle-perftools-dev on every non-22.04 runner including 24.04 (bab949a46), so this path is exercised there.

verdicts.corrected_claim: All svsim options and the C++ API used by simulation-driver.cpp remain valid, and -std=c++17 remains sufficient. '--trace' is still silently accepted as VCD. A grep of Changes 5.036 for timestamp and duplicate finds no entry for it. v5.036 verilated_vcd_c.cpp:196 is `if (m_wrTimeEndp == m_writep) m_writep = m_wrTimeBeginp;` inside emitTimeChange, with the comment 'if last output was timestamp backup and overwrite it ... missed.claim: 'Set trigger vector in whole words (#5857)', Changes 5.036 'Optimize trigger vector in whole words'. Triggers are now set as whole 64-bit words when triggerBitIdx is word-aligned and there are 64 or more triggers, instead of bit by bit. This changes the generated code, and it renames the runtime VlTriggerVec::set to setBit and adds setWord.
missed.evidence: Commit 59cb53cfb (2025-03-14). Its message says it improves C++ compile times by ~4x on some large designs and has a minor run-time performance benefit. v5.036 V3Sched.cpp:504, :515 and :656 use "setBit" and :756 uses "setWord". v5.036 include/verilated_types.h VlTriggerVec has setWord and setBit. The V3Sched.cpp:757 whole-word path applies only per full 64-trigger word. The new test is t_scheduling_many_clocks.
missed.impact: Negligible for single-clock Chisel designs, which have far fewer than 64 triggers, so they take the unchanged bit-wise path. It is relevant only for designs with many triggers or many clocks. Generated code and runtime must come from the same version, which they do when verilator and its include/ directory are the same install.

missed.claim: 'Add numactl-like automatic assignment of processor affinity (#5911)'. VlThreadPool's constructor now calls numaAssign(), which reads /proc/cpuinfo and calls pthread_setaffinity_np. It is a no-op ('too few threads') unless the model uses 2 or more worker threads. verilated_threads.cpp is always in the verilated runtime file list.
missed.evidence: Commit 6d1e82b90 (2025-04-02). v5.036 include/verilated_threads.cpp: VlThreadPool::VlThreadPool calls numaAssign(), which returns 'running under numactl' if the affinity mask is partial, 'too few threads' if num_threads < 2, and 'too many threads' if num_threads > hardware_concurrency. V3Global::verilatedCppFiles() (new in this range) always lists verilated_threads.cpp. verilatedos_c.h gains VlOs::getcpu using sched_getcpu.
missed.impact: None for this project: svsim does not pass --threads, so no VlThreadPool is created (V3EmitCModel.cpp:512 and V3EmitCSyms.cpp:799 use the context's pool only for multithreaded models). The new code is compiled into every model build at -std=c++17 (it uses sched.h and <fstream> but needs no newer standard). It is only a build-time cost and cannot change simulation results.

missed.claim: Several scheduling/optimizer bug fixes in the range touch code that every design goes through, but each is aimed at a corner case that firtool-style synchronous RTL is unlikely to hit. They are: V3MergeCond treats branching statements (disable/return/break) as fences (#5811/#5814); V3SenExprBuilder no longer uses function locals and has its variable caches invalidated correctly (#5822, #5834/#5835), which matters only when a trigger-evaluation function gets split by --output-split-cfuncs; V3Const sorts wide SenItems with isLtXZ (#5816); V3Gate tolerates a circular-logic edge that became non-circular (#5889/#5898); V3Delayed relaxes the 'Malformed LHS in NBA' assertion to isPure() (#5904); the out-of-range lvalue select width fix (#5820).
missed.evidence: Commits 14f618b0f, fc302a520, 0133bc6b0, 96bffd49a, 39c3e79a3, f3684a85b, 51fcb881d, all inside v5.034..v5.036. missed.impact: Probably none. These remove internal errors (assertion aborts) or miscompiles in unusual constructs. If a ChiselSim build ever failed with an internal-error assertion on older versions, they are a candidate explanation for a difference.
